text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government warns Zambians against straying into war-ravaged Zaire because it cannot guarantee their safety.
- Environment minister William Harrigton asks donors to help the country fight the hyacinth weed choking the Kafue river.
- Journalists recommend the formation of a self-regulatory body headed by a judge to help the media uphold ethical standards.
- The World Trade Organisation says Zambia recorded the highest growth rate in the tourism sector on the African continent with an increase of 62 percent in 1996.
- The attorney general attempts to block the Examination Council of Zambia from giving evidence in a case in which opposition parties are challenging president Frederick Chiluba's credentials.
